"Create a modern-day fictional President Simulator game where the player becomes the leader of a country and has full responsibility for governing and developing the nation.

Core Gameplay

The player acts as President and manages every major aspect of the country:

- Government: Appoint, dismiss, and replace ministers. Manage the cabinet, ministries, parliament, and political parties.
- Economy: Manage GDP, taxes, inflation, unemployment, national debt, treasury, imports, exports, and national budget.
- Military: Manage army, air force, navy, personnel, weapons, military bases, defence spending, recruitment, and procurement.
- Diplomacy: Interact with other countries, establish alliances, sign treaties, negotiate trade deals, impose sanctions, and manage international relations.
- Infrastructure: Build roads, factories, hospitals, schools, power plants, ports, and military facilities.
- Intelligence: Manage intelligence agencies, national security, espionage reports, and internal threats.
- Domestic Politics: Manage public approval, elections, protests, opposition parties, corruption, and national stability.

Fictional World

Create an entire fictional modern world containing multiple independent countries. Each country should have its own leader, government, economy, military, resources, political interests, and diplomatic relationships.

Other countries should operate independently and make decisions. They can develop economically, form alliances, start conflicts, experience political crises, and interact with the player's nation.

Dynamic Events

Generate ongoing events such as economic crises, cabinet scandals, military threats, diplomatic negotiations, border tensions, elections, protests, international conflicts, and natural disasters.

Present these events through interactive news reports, minister briefings, intelligence documents, and presidential decisions.

Every decision should have meaningful consequences.

Gameplay Interface

Make this primarily a UI-based strategy simulator, not a 3D game.

Use a professional modern government dashboard with:

- Presidential overview.
- National statistics.
- Interactive economic charts.
- Cabinet and ministry management.
- Military command interface.
- International relations.
- Country profiles.
- News and notifications.
- Presidential decision popups.

Use a polished dark navy interface with subtle gold accents, professional typography, detailed statistics, and modern strategy-game aesthetics.

Simulation Mechanics

Implement a working game-time system with pause, normal speed, and fast-forward.

All systems must be interconnected. For example, increasing military spending affects the national budget, economic crises affect public approval, diplomatic relationships affect trade, and infrastructure investments improve economic development.

The player should be able to save and continue their game.

Main Objective

There is no fixed winning condition. The player creates their own political legacy.

Become an economic superpower, build the strongest military, establish a global alliance, dominate international trade, maintain a stable democracy, or become an authoritarian ruler.

Make this a genuinely playable, deep, interactive nation-management simulator rather than a collection of decorative dashboards. Prioritize functional gameplay mechanics and interconnected systems.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Playable browser President Simulator: implementation checklist

### Core loop
- [ ] Start with a fictional country, a four-year term (48 months), and a short briefing of its inherited conditions.
- [ ] Each month: review dashboard → respond to an event or choose a policy → advance month → resolve systems → show a results summary.
- [ ] Win by reaching the end of the term with the government intact; lose early if removed from office, the treasury defaults, or the military stages a coup.
- [ ] Display the causes of major changes so the player can understand consequences.

### Interconnected monthly systems
- [ ] **Economy:** track GDP, growth, inflation, unemployment, tax revenue, spending, debt, and treasury. Revenue and spending change the treasury; deficits increase debt. Inflation and unemployment affect approval.
- [ ] **Budget:** allocate a monthly budget across healthcare, education, infrastructure, defense, and welfare. Make trade-offs visible; spending above revenue contributes to the deficit.
- [ ] **Politics:** track public approval, governing-coalition support, legislative seats, and election timing. Approval responds to jobs, prices, services, crises, and policy decisions. Low coalition support blocks legislation; elections can change seat balance.
- [ ] **Military and security:** track readiness, loyalty, and internal stability. Defense funding improves readiness; low stability or loyalty raises coup risk. Avoid random instant failure—warn the player as risk rises.
- [ ] **Diplomacy:** track relations with a few neighboring countries and one major power. Actions can improve trade or aid, but harm relations with rivals; poor relations may trigger sanctions or border incidents.
- [ ] **Events and decisions:** offer one consequential event most months, with 2–3 choices. Choices change multiple systems, have readable immediate effects, and may set flags for later events.
- [ ] **Longer-term outcomes:** resolve policy effects over several months (for example, infrastructure spending boosts growth after a delay). Keep a small number of active effects visible.

### Starter constants
Use a fictional setting and tune these after playtesting.

| Setting | Starting value / rule |
|---|---:|
| Term length | 48 months |
| Starting treasury | 12% of GDP |
| Starting debt | 55% of GDP |
| Starting monthly revenue | 3.0% of GDP |
| Monthly budget allocation | 3.0% of GDP, adjustable |
| Starting GDP growth | 0.3% per month |
| Starting inflation | 0.4% per month |
| Starting unemployment | 8% |
| Starting approval | 52 / 100 |
| Starting coalition support | 58 / 100 |
| Starting military readiness | 60 / 100 |
| Starting military loyalty | 70 / 100 |
| Starting stability | 65 / 100 |
| Starting foreign relations | 0 / 100 per country |
| Approval/support/stability bounds | 0–100 |
| Monthly event frequency | 1 event; occasional quiet month |
| Default game-over thresholds | Treasury below −5% GDP; stability below 10; coup risk reaches 100 |
| Coup risk | Rise with low loyalty/stability and prolonged unrest; fall with credible reforms and adequate funding |

Treat these as design starting points, not historical forecasts. Clamp percentages and indices to sensible bounds, and avoid letting a single routine choice create an unrecoverable state.

### UI screens
- [ ] **Briefing / new game:** country overview, difficulty, and start button.
- [ ] **Dashboard:** month, treasury, debt, GDP, approval, coalition support, stability, alerts, and next-month button.
- [ ] **Budget:** adjustable allocations with totals, projected deficit, and plain-language effects.
- [ ] **Politics:** coalition/seat view, upcoming elections, and legislation or reform actions.
- [ ] **Military & diplomacy:** readiness, loyalty, relations, and available actions.
- [ ] **Events:** decision text, choices, and concise previews of likely consequences.
- [ ] **History / report:** monthly change log, important decisions, election results, and end-of-term outcome.
- [ ] **Save/load:** save from the dashboard and resume on reload; clearly indicate whether a save exists.

### Save and implementation checks
- [ ] Save a versioned state object: month, country stats, budget, relations, coalition/seats, active effects, event flags, and history.
- [ ] Use browser storage; validate loaded data and fall back safely if the save is missing, malformed, or from an unsupported version.
- [ ] Keep state updates deterministic for a given state and choice, except for seeded event selection; this makes saves and debugging reliable.
- [ ] Test a normal term, election loss, default risk, coup-risk warnings, repeated saves/loads, and boundary values.
- [ ] Ensure all key actions work with keyboard and touch, and show confirmation or explanation for irreversible decisions.
</subagent>

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable fictional President Simulator with interconnected nation-management systems and a polished strategy dashboard.

## Requirements
- Cover government, economy, military, diplomacy, infrastructure, intelligence, and domestic politics.
- Include an autonomous fictional world, consequential dynamic events, game-time controls, and save/continue.
- Use a dark navy UI with gold accents and make the game playable without a fixed victory condition.

## Decisions
- Use a vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript app at the repository root.
- Set the player nation as Veloria, with monthly simulation and a 48-month election cycle.

## Work State
### Completed
